# Crypto Alternative Data for the Jetson Trader: What Works, What's Free, What's Blocked

All endpoint claims below were **empirically verified today from this US network** (curl from the dev Mac; same geo-class as the Jetson).

## 0. Critical access facts (verified 2026-06-10)

| Source | Status from US IP | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fapi.binance.com` (live funding/OI) | **HTTP 451 blocked** | Confirms ccxt #15891: Binance blocks even public reads from US |
| `data.binance.vision` archive | **200 OK** | Monthly `fundingRate` zips ≥ 2020-01; daily `metrics` (5-min OI + long/short ratios) ≥ 2021-06; SOLUSDT metrics ≥ 2022-01 |
| `api.bybit.com` | **CloudFront country block** | Unusable |
| `www.okx.com/api/v5` | **Works, no key** | Live funding (`/public/funding-rate`), OI (`/public/open-interest`), liquidation orders, spot tickers — all 6 symbols (BTC/ETH/XRP/SOL/DOGE/LINK-USDT-SWAP) listed |
| OKX funding-rate-history / rubik OI-history | Works but **shallow** (empty before ~2025) | Not usable for training history |
| Hyperliquid `api.hyperliquid.xyz/info` | Works, no key | Hourly funding+premium+OI, history since mid-2023; good live fallback |
| Kraken Futures `historicalfundingrates` | Works, no key | Hourly relative funding, multi-year |
| Deribit public API | Works | BTC/ETH 8h funding |
| Coin Metrics Community API | **Works, no key** | 31 free daily BTC metrics incl. `CapMVRVCur` (MVRV) and `FlowInExUSD`/`FlowOutExUSD` (aggregate exchange flows) |
| DefiLlama `stablecoins.llama.fi` | Works, no key | Daily stablecoin circulating supply back to 2017 |
| Coinbase Exchange + Kraken public | Work | Enables free Coinbase-premium computation |
| Coinglass API | **No free tier** ($29/mo Hobbyist) | Skip; use OKX liquidation-orders instead |
| Glassnode/CryptoQuant flows | Paywalled (flows = Pro tiers) | Coin Metrics community replaces them |

**Architecture conclusion:** train on Binance archive dumps (free, deep, point-in-time exact), serve live from OKX REST, fall back to Hyperliquid/Kraken. Binance live REST is not an option from a US Jetson.

## 1. Funding rates — strongest evidence, build first

**Evidence (established):** BIS WP 1087 / Management Science 2024 (Schmeling, Schrimpf, Todorov, "Crypto Carry"): perp funding/basis averages >10% p.a. (peaks 40-60%), and **high carry predicts future price crashes** — exactly the 12-48h crowded-long-unwind channel you'd feed the ensemble. The Oct 10-11 2025 cascade postmortem (SSRN 5611392) documents the leverage→funding-skew→cascade sequence on hourly data. Caveat (established): pure carry alpha has decayed — arXiv 2510.14435 reports carry Sharpe 6.45 over 2020-2025 falling to 4.06 from 2024 and **negative in 2025**. So treat funding as a *positioning/crash-risk feature and gate*, not standalone alpha; let the existing policy-level backtest gate decide.

**Training data:** `data.binance.vision/data/futures/um/monthly/fundingRate/{SYM}USDT/*.zip` — 8h funding since 2020-01 for BTC/ETH/XRP/LINK (later listings for SOL/DOGE), ~6 years ≫ the 3-year requirement. Point-in-time is exact: each rate is known at its funding timestamp (00/08/16 UTC); forward-fill onto the bar grid.

**Live:** poll OKX `/api/v5/public/funding-rate?instId=BTC-USDT-SWAP` each crypto-loop cycle (returns current + next predicted rate — the *predicted* next rate is the freshest positioning signal). Map `BTC/USD → BTC-USDT-SWAP`, etc.

**Features (harvest):** `funding_rate` (annualized), `funding_z30d` (30-day rolling z), `funding_chg_24h`, `funding_extreme` (|z|>2 flag). **Gate:** if funding_z > +2 while long (crowded long) → halve new-entry size via the existing advisory tilt; symmetric for shorts if ever enabled. **Train/serve skew:** Binance-vs-OKX funding levels differ slightly; z-score per venue (and optionally validate on the ~1y of OKX history available) to neutralize.

**Timing effect (weak/practitioner):** documented position-flattening and U-shaped vol inside the 8h cycle; cheap to add `mins_to_funding` as a feature — don't expect much.

## 2. Open interest + liquidations

**Evidence:** academically OI predicts *volatility/fragility* more than direction; the cascade literature (SSRN 5611392; exchange microstructure write-ups) consistently flags **OI spike (~+20%/48h) + extreme funding** as the pre-cascade signature. Best used as an interaction feature and a risk gate.

**Training data:** `data.binance.vision/.../daily/metrics/{SYM}USDT/` — 5-minute `sum_open_interest`, `sum_open_interest_value`, plus top-trader and global long/short ratios, ≥2021-06 (BTC), ≥2022-01 (SOL). ~4.5 years free. The live Binance `openInterestHist` REST only keeps 30 days *and* is geo-blocked — the archive is the only free deep source; grab it now and cron-sync daily (~few MB/day zipped).

**Live:** OKX `/api/v5/public/open-interest?instId=...` per cycle; OKX `/public/liquidation-orders` (verified working) as a real-time cascade tripwire (no free aggregated Coinglass feed — their API has **no free tier**, confirmed on pricing page).

**Features:** `oi_chg_4h`, `oi_chg_24h`, `oi_z30d`, and `oi_z * funding_z` interaction. **Gate:** OI 48h change > +20% AND funding_z > 2 → block new crypto entries until reset (extends the existing circuit breaker).

## 3. On-chain: what's actually evidenced and free

- **Stablecoin exchange inflows / supply growth — best evidenced at your horizon.** Peer-reviewed (arXiv 2411.06327, sample 2017-2023): USDT net inflows to exchanges **positively predict BTC and ETH returns at 1-6h intervals** and negatively predict vol. Free proxies: (a) DefiLlama daily aggregate stablecoin supply → 1/7-day mint/burn delta as a risk-appetite tilt (you already poll for depeg — reuse that plumbing); (b) Coin Metrics community `FlowInExUSD−FlowOutExUSD` for BTC/ETH daily netflow. Both daily-lagged → lag 1 day in harvest exactly like the sentiment feature.
- **MVRV/SOPR — cycle-scale, not 12-48h.** The supporting study (Sharpe 0.45→1.28 with MVRV-Z timing) is multi-*month* cycle timing; standalone out-of-sample evidence at short horizons is weak/data-mined. If used at all: Coin Metrics `CapMVRVCur` (free, verified) as a slow regime tilt input to the HMM/tilt stack, never as a fast feature. SOPR is not in the free tier — skip.
- **Exchange BTC netflow (coins)** — evidence mixed; volatility-linked. Cheap to include since it ships in the same Coin Metrics call.

## 4. Cross-exchange basis & BTC dominance

- **Coinbase premium** (practitioner evidence via CryptoQuant: negative-premium streaks precede corrections, positive flips precede 4-8 week strength; no rigorous OOS academic test). Free live computation, verified: Coinbase `BTC-USD` ticker vs OKX `BTC-USDT` × Kraken `USDT/USD`. Use as a daily-context tilt input; historical backfill possible from Coinbase candles + Binance vision klines if it earns its keep.
- **BTC dominance / alt rotation:** academic lead-lag BTC↔ETH is *bi-directional* (Research in International Business & Finance 2019) — weak as alpha. Cheapest implementation: **ETH/BTC ratio momentum and per-alt vs-BTC relative strength computed from Alpaca bars you already have** (mirrors the existing SPY-BTC feature). Zero new data dependencies; worth one feature column each.

## 5. Sessions / seasonality

Established: **volatility and volume are reliably lower on weekends; mean-return day-of-week effects are unstable/contradictory across samples** (2014-2024 weekend-effect study: no detectable return gap; calendar-anomaly studies find moments effects, not exploitable means). Action: add cyclical hour-of-day/day-of-week encodings + `is_weekend` as *features* (let LightGBM find vol/liquidity structure, helps the GARCH vol-targeting), and consider widening assumed spread cost on weekends; do **not** build directional seasonal rules.

## 6. Strongest 2-4 for 12-48h + integration order

1. **Funding rate level/extremes** (BIS/Management Science crash-prediction — strongest primary evidence).
2. **OI change + funding×OI interaction** (cascade-fragility evidence; same downloader).
3. **Stablecoin exchange-inflow/supply delta** (peer-reviewed 1-6h→daily predictive evidence; trivially free).
4. **Coinbase premium** (practitioner-grade; free; tilt-only until it proves out in the policy backtest).

All four enter harvest as point-in-time-safe features (funding/OI timestamped intraday; on-chain lagged 1 day) **and** the top two double as live entry gates. Historical depth: funding 6 yrs, OI 4.5 yrs, stablecoins 8 yrs — the 3-year training requirement is met free of charge. Memory footprint: a daily REST poll + ~50-100 MB of cached parquet — negligible beside the 2.5 GB stack.
topRecommendations: 1. Build a `derivs_data.py` module + backfill job pulling Binance archive funding (data.binance.vision monthly fundingRate zips, 2020→now, ~6 calls/symbol) and 5-min OI metrics dumps (2021-06→now); cache as parquet. Add 4 funding features (level, 30d z-score, 24h change, |z|>2 flag) and 3 OI features (4h/24h change, 30d z) + funding_z×oi_z interaction to harvest for all 6 cryptos. Effort: 1.5-2 days. Impact: first non-price feature family with primary-source evidence (BIS WP1087: high carry predicts crashes) at exactly the 12-48h horizon; expect the largest single feature-importance shift of any wave-2 item.

2. Live serving from OKX (verified US-accessible, no key): poll /api/v5/public/funding-rate and /public/open-interest per crypto-loop cycle with BTC/USD→BTC-USDT-SWAP mapping; z-score per venue to kill Binance-train/OKX-serve skew; Hyperliquid + Kraken Futures as verified fallbacks. Effort: 0.5-1 day. Impact: makes rec 1 deployable; the OKX 'next predicted funding rate' field is the freshest positioning signal available free.

3. Crowding/cascade gate in crypto_loop: block or halve new long entries when funding_z30d > +2 AND OI 48h change > +20% (the documented pre-cascade signature from the Oct-2025 liquidation postmortem); wire into the existing advisory tilt clamp + circuit breaker. Effort: 0.5 day on top of recs 1-2. Impact: tail-risk reduction on the exact crowded-long-unwind events that dominate crypto drawdowns; cheap to validate in the existing policy-level backtest gate.

4. Stablecoin mint/burn risk-appetite feature: daily DefiLlama stablecoincharts aggregate supply (free, no key, history to 2017) → 1d/7d supply-growth deltas, lagged 1 day point-in-time (reuse the existing depeg-check plumbing and the sentiment-feature lag pattern). Effort: 0.5 day. Impact: peer-reviewed support (arXiv 2411.06327: USDT exchange inflows positively predict BTC/ETH returns at 1-6h intervals); slow tilt + harvest feature.

5. Coin Metrics Community API daily features (verified free, no key): BTC/ETH exchange netflow (FlowInExUSD−FlowOutExUSD) as 1-day-lagged harvest features, and CapMVRVCur (MVRV) as a slow input to the HMM/regime tilt only — never as a fast 12-48h feature (evidence is cycle-scale). Effort: 0.5-1 day. Impact: modest; ships in one API call alongside rec 4.

6. Zero-data-cost regime features from existing Alpaca bars: ETH/BTC ratio momentum (alt-rotation/risk-appetite) and per-alt vs-BTC relative strength, mirroring the existing SPY-BTC feature; plus cyclical hour-of-day/day-of-week + is_weekend encodings (established lower weekend vol/liquidity — helps GARCH vol-targeting and LightGBM, not directional rules). Effort: 2-4 hours. Impact: small but free; improves regime conditioning.

7. Coinbase premium live tilt: compute (Coinbase BTC-USD) / (OKX BTC-USDT × Kraken USDT/USD) − 1 every cycle (all three endpoints verified free/no-key); feed as advisory tilt input; only invest in historical backfill (Coinbase candles + Binance vision klines) if the live A/B and policy backtest justify it. Effort: 0.5 day live, +1 day backfill. Impact: practitioner-grade US-demand signal; treat as unproven until gated.

8. Cron-sync data.binance.vision daily (funding + metrics zips, few MB/day) so training history keeps accruing even if the archive ever gets geo-blocked like fapi/Bybit did; log a loud alert on first 451/403 from any live data source (fail-closed to price-only features). Effort: 2-3 hours. Impact: protects the new feature family's future retrains.

9. Add OKX /public/liquidation-orders polling as a live-only cascade tripwire metric in the trade journal (no free history exists — Coinglass has no free API tier, verified) — measure first, gate later if the journal shows liquidation bursts precede your stop-outs. Effort: 0.5 day. Impact: measurement now, optional gate later.

10. Validation discipline for the whole family: funding-carry alpha decayed to negative in 2025 (arXiv 2510.14435) — so run recs 1-4 through the existing purged-CV + DSR holdout + policy-backtest promotion gate as ONE feature-family experiment (ablation: price-only vs +derivs vs +derivs+onchain) before any live tilt goes active. Effort: 1 day of pipeline runs. Impact: prevents shipping a decayed signal as if it were the 2021 version.

# Equity Event-Awareness: Findings for the Trader System

## Headline
The system's biggest unpriced event risk is the 2-position overnight sleeve (`stock_loop.py:_select_overnight_keepers`, ~line 216) holding through earnings prints with GTC stops that gap straight through. The biggest *misconception* to avoid: blanket macro-day stand-downs would sacrifice the best risk-adjusted hours of the year (Savor-Wilson). PEAD is dead in this universe's cap range — earnings work here is risk management, not alpha.

## 1. Earnings (strongest evidence, highest priority)
**Gap risk.** Universe names routinely price 5–15% implied earnings moves (NVDA/TSLA ~5–10%, MSTR ~6% last print) and realize 20%+ tails: SMCI gained **+24.5%** the day after its 2026-05-05 report (Market Chameleon); ENPH/ROKU/AFRM-class names have comparable downside gaps. Math vs. the current risk model: sleeve cap is 5% equity/position (`OVERNIGHT_SLEEVE_MAX_PCT_EQUITY=0.05`); a 20% adverse gap = **-1.0% equity on one name, -2%+ if both keepers report same week — 2–4x the 0.5% per-trade risk budget**, and the GTC stop fills at the open, not the stop price. The sleeve currently has *no* earnings filter (verified: only leveraged-ETF, pred, and cap filters exist).

**PEAD in the 2020s: do NOT trade it.** Martineau (Critical Finance Review, 2022, "Rest in Peace Post-Earnings Announcement Drift") shows PEAD ≈ **zero for large caps since 2006**, disappearing from all non-microcaps since ~2001 (decimalization/Reg-NMS/HFT price discovery on announcement day). Katz-McCubbins-McMullin further show firm-level PEADs are heterogeneous and non-monotonic — the portfolio-level anomaly is partly an aggregation artifact. Cross-checked against 2024 work still finding PEAD only in attention-limited/small-cap or non-US settings. For this 46-name large/mid-cap book: no PEAD module.

**Holding through the print is not clearly -EV** (Frazzini-Lamont earnings-announcement premium ~60bp/month long-announcers, NBER w13090), but the variance is incompatible with 0.5%-risk-to-stop sizing and a 2-slot sleeve. Policy: **exclude from sleeve, don't avoid day-trading after the print** (announcement-day price discovery is complete by open per Martineau; volume/vol are high, which the entry models can trade).

**Data source (verified):** Finnhub `/calendar/earnings` is on the free tier (60 calls/min; client method `earnings_calendar(_from, to, symbol)` in finnhub-python — the project already instantiates this client in `sentiment.py:_get_finnhub()`). One unfiltered call per day for a 14-day window returns all US earnings incl. BMO/AMC `hour` field; cache to JSON with 24h TTL. Alpaca corporate actions does **not** carry earnings dates (dividends/splits/mergers only — confirmed in Alpaca docs). yfinance earnings dates are documented-unreliable (wrong dates, future dates broken — yfinance issues #2559/#2566); use only as cross-check. For *historical* earnings dates to backfill model features, use SEC EDGAR `data.sec.gov/submissions/` 8-K (Item 2.02) dates — free, point-in-time, and the system already has EDGAR plumbing.

**Policy (concrete):**
- Sleeve: skip any symbol with earnings between today's close and the next open (+1 day buffer for date ambiguity). ~10 LOC in `_select_overnight_keepers`.
- No N-day pre-earnings entry blackout needed for day trades (flattened by 3:50 anyway).
- Optional: halve clip size on the trading day *after* a name's print — daily ATR(14)/GARCH lag the 3–5x realized-vol expansion by a day.
- Add `days_to_next_earnings` (clipped 0–10) and `is_post_print_day` features; retrain passes through the existing DSR/backtest gates.

## 2. Macro calendar (FOMC/CPI/NFP)
**Pre-FOMC drift is dead:** Lucca-Moench (NY Fed sr512) found +49bp in the 24h pre-FOMC (1994–2011, ~80% of the equity premium), but Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert (Finance Research Letters 2021) show it **essentially disappeared after 2015**. Don't build a drift trade.
**Announcement days pay:** Savor-Wilson (JFE 2014): announcement-day (CPI/employment/FOMC) excess returns **11.4bp vs 1.1bp** on other days, **~10x Sharpe**, 1958–2009. A long-biased bot should *not* stand down all day.
**But intraday vol clusters at the release:** FOMC days run ~60% more volatile (SPX ~2.0% avg range vs 1.25%); the 14:00 statement + 14:30 presser overlaps the bot's 14:30–15:30 entry window — entries there buy the most whipsaw-prone half hour. CPI/NFP (08:30 ET, pre-open) feed the 9:30 open the system already trades; evidence supports trading it at reduced size rather than skipping.
**Policy:** static `macro_calendar.json` — FOMC dates are published through **2027** (next: 2026-06-16/17, statement 14:00 ET) on federalreserve.gov; CPI and Employment Situation dates published a year ahead on bls.gov/schedule (BLS blocks bots — verified 403 — so hand-refresh ~25 dates once a year; add a unit test failing when <30 days of calendar remain). On FOMC days: suppress 14:30–15:00 entries (or shift window to 15:00–15:45) and don't tighten trailing stops 13:55–14:45. On CPI/NFP days: 0.5x size multiplier for the first 30–45 min, fed through the existing advisory tilt (`TILT_MIN/MAX`, `strategy_config.py:49`).

## 3. Rebalances, witching, TOM, tax-loss
- **Russell reconstitution is now semiannual (June + November) starting 2026** (CME/LSEG) — recon Friday close is among the year's largest volume events ($114.7B NYSE + $102.5B Nasdaq closing auctions in 2025); effects concentrate in the closing auction and adds/deletes (small caps: QBTS, POET, RDW, SERV, PRME, ASTS are candidates). Action: exclude small-cap names from the sleeve on the 2 recon Fridays; zero cost.
- **Triple witching:** evidence mixed — avg OPEX-day return 0.03% vs 0.04% random days (QuantifiedStrategies); volume spike real, return effect weak. Action: optionally add the 4 quad-witching Fridays to the sleeve-blackout list; nothing more.
- **Turn-of-month:** largely gone in 2010s–2020s US large caps (Quantseeker et al.); conditional revivals are not robust enough to act on. Skip.
- **Tax-loss/January:** real historically (small>large +2.1% in January, AQR 1926–2017) but long-only system with weekly retrain captures any residual via momentum features. Skip.

## 4. Short interest / squeeze risk (verified free source)
**Live-tested:** `POST https://api.finra.org/data/group/otcMarket/name/consolidatedShortInterest` with `compareFilters` on `symbolCode`+`settlementDate` — **no API key, HTTP 200**, returns `daysToCoverQuantity`, `currentShortPositionQuantity`, `averageDailyVolumeQuantity`. Current data confirmed: MSTR 2026-05-29 settlement = 37.68M shares short, DTC 2.82. Biweekly settlements, published ~9 business days later (use settlement-date lag for point-in-time correctness in features). One bulk call per cycle (limit 5000, filter locally) — 2 calls/month.
**Evidence:** Hong-Li-Ni-Scheinkman-Yan (NBER w21166): DTC long-short spread **1.2%/month**; high-DTC names underperform but carry two-sided tails (squeeze melt-ups break trailing-stop logic; crashes gap stops). Practitioner threshold: DTC > 8 = squeeze-prone.
**Policy:** nightly-cached DTC + ΔSI% per name; (a) sleeve-exclude DTC > 8 or SI%-of-ADV extreme names; (b) 0.5–0.75x size tilt on high-DTC longs via the advisory tilt; (c) feed `dtc` and `si_change_pct` as model features (biweekly step function — lag to publication date).

## 5. Analyst revisions — skip on current data
Post-revision drift is real but front-loaded: recent work finds most of the reaction inside the first 5–15 minutes, with the classic multi-month drift (Womack: +2.4% buys/-9.1% sells over 6 months) reflecting pre-2000s markets. Finnhub free tier only gives `recommendation_trends` (monthly aggregates — far too slow for 1–5-day drift); event-time `upgrade_downgrade` and price targets are premium, and Finnhub has a history of migrating endpoints to premium (GitHub issue #271). Verdict: **no reliable free event-time feed → don't build**; the existing news-sentiment pipeline already partially captures upgrade headlines.

## 6. Factor/sector exposure (no new data needed)
The book is effectively two bets: high-beta tech/semis and crypto-beta. Specific overlap the correlation penalty may underweight: the bot can hold BTC/ETH clips *and* MSTR+COIN+MARA+HOOD (all crypto proxies) simultaneously; semis bucket is NVDA/AMD/AVGO/ARM/MRVL/SMCI/SOXL (SOXL 3x). Cheap fixes, all from existing Alpaca bars: (1) rolling 60d beta vs SPY per name; cap Σ(position_weight×beta) for open stock clips at ~1.5–2.0 SPY-equivalents, scaling new entries when binding; (2) static 8-bucket sector map (46 names, JSON) with max ~40% of concurrent clips per bucket, counting crypto book notional inside the crypto-proxy bucket; (3) sleeve keepers must come from different buckets. Index-hedging the sleeve (short QQQ overnight) is possible on Alpaca paper but low value vs. a beta-diverse 2-name sleeve — defer.

## Cross-cutting note
All event gates should be **advisory-input or pre-entry filters that fail open on data outages** for entries but **fail closed for the sleeve** (no earnings data → flatten everything, the pre-sleeve status quo), preserving the existing fail-closed philosophy.
topRecommendations: 1. Earnings sleeve exclusion (DO FIRST): new events_calendar.py fetching Finnhub /calendar/earnings (existing key, free tier; 1 unfiltered 14-day-window call/day, 24h JSON cache) + ~10 LOC filter in stock_loop._select_overnight_keepers skipping any symbol reporting between today's close and next open (+1-day buffer); fail closed (no calendar -> no sleeve). Effort: 0.5 day. Impact: removes the single largest tail in the system — a 20% earnings gap on a 5%-equity keeper = -1% equity, 2-4x the per-trade risk budget, unprotected by GTC stops (SMCI moved +24.5% on its May 2026 print).

2. Static macro_calendar.json (FOMC dates from federalreserve.gov, published through 2027; CPI + Employment Situation from bls.gov/schedule, hand-refreshed yearly — BLS blocks bots, verified 403) + unit test failing when <30 days of calendar remain. On FOMC days suppress 14:30-15:00 entries (statement 14:00, presser 14:30) and pause trailing-stop tightening 13:55-14:45; on CPI/NFP days apply 0.5x size via the existing advisory tilt for the first 30-45 min. Do NOT stand down whole days (Savor-Wilson: announcement days earn 11.4bp vs 1.1bp, ~10x Sharpe). Effort: 1 day. Impact: cuts whipsaw stop-outs in the worst 30-60 min/month while keeping the announcement premium.

3. FINRA days-to-cover squeeze guard: nightly job POSTing api.finra.org/data/group/otcMarket/name/consolidatedShortInterest (live-tested, free, no key; returns daysToCoverQuantity per symbol per biweekly settlementDate). Sleeve-exclude and 0.5-0.75x size-tilt names with DTC > 8; log DTC on every entry. Effort: 0.5-1 day. Impact: trims two-sided squeeze/crash tails in MSTR/IONQ/QBTS-class names; Hong et al. show high-DTC names underperform (1.2%/month L-S spread) so the long-side filter is mildly +EV.

4. Sector-bucket + beta-dollar exposure caps (no new data): rolling 60d beta vs SPY from existing Alpaca bars; cap book beta-weighted stock exposure at ~1.5-2.0 SPY-equivalents; static 8-bucket map with max ~40% concurrent clips per bucket, counting live crypto notional inside the crypto-proxy bucket (MSTR/COIN/MARA/HOOD overlap with BTC book); require sleeve keepers from distinct buckets. Effort: 1 day. Impact: converts a hidden one-factor book into measured exposure; biggest effect on drawdown clustering, complements existing correlation penalty.

5. Earnings-relative model features: days_to_next_earnings (clipped 0-10) and is_post_print_day, backfilled point-in-time from SEC EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 dates (data.sec.gov/submissions, free; system already has EDGAR plumbing) with Finnhub forward calendar for live; passes through existing purged-CV/DSR/backtest gates. Effort: 1-2 days incl. backfill + retrain validation. Impact: lets LSTM/LGBM condition on the known vol-regime cycle around prints instead of being surprised by it.

6. Post-print vol haircut: 0.5x clip size on the first trading day after a name reports (daily ATR(14)/GARCH lag the 3-5x realized-vol expansion by ~1 day). Piggybacks on item 1's calendar cache. Effort: 1-2 hours. Impact: right-sizes the highest-variance day trades the bot takes.

7. Sleeve blackout date list: exclude small-cap names (QBTS/POET/RDW/SERV/PRME/ASTS) from the sleeve on the 2 Russell reconstitution Fridays (semiannual June+November from 2026, CME/LSEG) and optionally all names on the 4 quad-witching Fridays. Effort: 30 minutes (config list). Impact: small but free — avoids closing-auction distortion nights ($100B+ auction days).

8. Do NOT build a PEAD module: Martineau (Critical Finance Review 2022) shows PEAD ~zero in large caps since 2006; Katz et al. show firm-level drift is non-monotonic. Any PEAD-flavored signal should be rejected by your DSR gate — don't spend the research budget. Effort saved: ~1 week.

9. Skip analyst-revision momentum on current data: Finnhub free tier only exposes monthly recommendation_trends (too slow for the 1-5 day drift); event-time upgrade/downgrade is premium and the drift is front-loaded into minutes in modern markets. # Label Engineering & Meta-Labeling: Implementation Plan for This Pipeline

## 0. The system-specific headline finding

Your stock labels are structurally wrong for your stock policy. `harvest_stock_data.py` builds `Target_Return_{12..48}` on RTH hourly bars = **1.8–7.4 trading-day** forward returns, but `stock_loop.py` flattens at 15:50 ET, so a 9:30–11:00 entry lives **≤6.3 hours** and a 14:30–15:30 entry **≤1.3 hours** (only a 2-name sleeve survives overnight). The model is optimized to predict returns the policy cannot harvest. Crypto labels are closer (24/7), but the 2.5x-ATR stop / 2:1 TP / trailing stack still truncates most fb-bar paths — `backtest.py` exit-reason counts will show what fraction of trades never reach fb bars. Fixing label/exit alignment is the cheapest expected-value item in this entire research wave.

## 1. Triple-barrier (TBL) matched to your exact exit stack

**Evidence.** AFML ch.3 defines TBL (first touch of profit-take/stop/vertical barrier). A 2025 peer-reviewed study on Binance BTC/ETH tick data (2018–2023, 5 expanding-window test quarters, XGBoost + 6 deep nets) found **CUSUM-sampled + triple-barrier labels were the only combination "achieving consistently positive trading performance even after accounting for transaction costs"**, beating time bars + next-bar prediction (Financial Innovation, Springer). A Korean-markets study (arXiv 2504.02249; 8.6M daily samples) used tuned barriers (9%, 29d vertical; label mix 35/29/36% TP/SL/time) reaching AUC 0.62. Practitioner comparisons (AXLFI blog — secondary source) report fixed-horizon strategies at -0.71%/76% maxDD vs TBL -0.03%/36.9% on identical data. Established: TBL ≥ fixed-horizon for downstream P&L; the rigorous head-to-head literature is thin but consistent in direction.

**Recipe for THIS system (don't use mlfinlab — you already own the exit engine).** Factor the inner exit loop of `backtest.simulate_ticker()` (lines ~193–227) into a pure function `exit_path(entry_i, opens, highs, lows, closes, atr, policy, is_last_bar_of_day, max_bars) -> (exit_i, gross_pct, reason)`, then:

- Label per bar t: run `exit_path` with `max_bars=fb` as the vertical barrier. Stop = `entry*(1 - clip(atr*atr_stop_mult/entry, stop_floor, stop_ceil))` (2.5x/floor 1.5% crypto; 2.0x/floor 1% stock), TP = `entry*(1 + min(tp_ceil, stop_dist*tp_rr))` — i.e., your live barriers ARE the AFML `pt_sl`, already volatility-scaled by ATR (equivalent to `get_daily_vol` scaling).
- **Vertical barrier: crypto = fb bars; stocks = min(fb bars, same-day last bar)** for the flattened 8-of-10 book. This is exactly mlfinlab's `add_vertical_barrier` semantics with an EOD override. Optionally emit a second stock label set with a T+1 vertical for the overnight-sleeve selector.
- Emit three columns per fb: `TB_Ret_{fb}` (gross path return at first touch — a *policy-consistent regression target*), `TB_Label_{fb}` (sign / {1,0,-1}), `TB_ExitBars_{fb}`. Keeping the continuous `TB_Ret` preserves your Huber-regression architecture; you don't have to switch to classification (see §6).
- Reusing one code path guarantees label==live-exit semantics permanently and de-risks drift between `strategy_config.py` and labels.

**Cost.** Vectorized per-ticker loop, O(N x avg-hold ≈ 20 bars): ~285k crypto + ~400k stock rows → <2 min on the Jetson CPU, run inside harvest. New columns ≈ 25 MB.

## 2. Meta-labeling — your policy backtester is the dataset generator (highest impact)

**Evidence.** Man & Chan (ICAIF 2020, QTS Capital, verified from the PDF): random-forest meta-model on **464 real strategy transactions** (153 features incl. implied/realized vol) lifted out-of-sample Sharpe **0.360 → 0.743** (no feature selection) → **0.829** (LIME-selected features), cumulative return 5.6% → 9.7% → 10.5%. The JFDS series (Joubert 2022; Meyer/Joubert/Alfeus 2022; Meyer/Barziy/Joubert 2023; Thumm/Barucca/Joubert 2022) establishes the framework: secondary binary classifier predicting "was the primary trade profitable", improving precision at modest recall cost, raising Sharpe and cutting maxDD; ensembles help most in multi-regime data. A crypto replication (Medium, BTC 1-min, LightGBM+Optuna+purged CV meta on Hilbert-cycle regime features over a Bollinger primary) turned **-44% into +53%** (H1-2022) — secondary source, but methodologically close to your stack. **Counterpoint** (QuantConnect, Baldisserri): meta-labeling fails when the secondary model sees the *same features* as an already-flexible end-to-end ML primary ("you cannot squeeze the same orange twice"). Your case avoids this trap structurally: the meta-label encodes the *path-dependent exit stack + fees* that the fb-return-trained primary never sees, and you can feed regime/cost features the primary doesn't use.

**Recipe.** Yes — replaying signals through the policy backtester is exactly the standard approach (Man & Chan used the strategy's own historical transaction log; H&T examples replay the primary).

1. `scripts/build_meta_dataset.py`: run `_predict_ticker` + `simulate_ticker` over **full history** (not 60d) with threshold lowered to ~0.5x `trade_threshold` (high-recall primary, per AFML), emitting one row per trade: `label = net_pct > 0`, plus entry-bar features: `predicted_return`, pred/ATR_Pct, `ATR_Pct`, `Volatility_12h`, RSI, BB width, Hurst, `Daily_Sentiment`, hour-of-day/entry-window id, |LSTM − LGB| disagreement, SPY-200d & HMM regime flags, VIX bucket, trailing 20-trade hit rate, bars-since-last-stop. Expect ~2–10k trades (crypto) — comfortably enough; Man & Chan used 464.
2. Leakage control: generate trades per walk-forward fold using that fold's predictions where feasible; at minimum train meta on a purged time split (your `get_walk_forward_folds` pattern) and report holdout-only metrics.
3. `meta_model.py`: LightGBM binary classifier (~15 features, depth ≤ 5) + isotonic calibration (`CalibratedClassifierCV`) — Meyer/Barziy/Joubert show calibration "significantly improves" fixed sizing methods (ECDF/SOPS-style fitted sizers don't need it).
4. Live: `predict_now.get_live_prediction` already returns a snapshot; compute meta_p in `base_loop` next to the LLM gate (lines ~1168–1176): **veto entry if meta_p < 0.5**; size via AFML ch.10: `z=(p−0.5)/sqrt(p(1−p)); m=2Φ(z)−1`, discretized in 0.05 steps (filters 60–80% of micro-adjustments per practitioner replication). Apply as its own multiplier beside `kelly_mult` (line ~1009), NOT inside the [0.1,1.3]-clamped tilt.
5. Retrain meta weekly after the primary in `run_pipeline.py`; gate it with the same policy backtest (meta-on vs meta-off comparison is one extra `simulate_ticker` pass).

**Cost.** Full-history replay = the expensive part: ~685k window inferences; batched on the Jetson GPU ≈ 10–25 min weekly (you already do similar volume in `train_lgb_ensemble`). Meta training: seconds, <100 MB.

## 3. CUSUM event sampling (Jetson-friendly)

**Evidence.** AFML ch.2: `S_t = max(0, S_{t-1} + y_t − E[y_t])`, sample when `S_t ≥ h`; avoids re-triggering while hovering (unlike BB touches). The Financial Innovation crypto paper tested CUSUM (1–3% thresholds) head-to-head vs 1h/12h/24h time bars: **CUSUM+TBL was the top performer net of costs**. Established directionally; exact effect size not stated in the open-access excerpt.

**Recipe.** `h` = EWMA daily vol (span ~100 bars) or fixed 0.75–1% crypto / 0.4–0.5% stock. Implement as a boolean `CUSUM_Event` column in harvest; in `hypersearch_v2.load_data`, intersect `_valid_indices` with event indices for TRAIN rows only (validation/holdout keep every bar so Sharpe/DSR stay comparable). Because `gather_windows` takes arbitrary indices, this is a ~20-line change. At h≈1x daily vol expect roughly 3–6x fewer training rows → 3–6x faster epochs (sub-linear wall-clock win after fixed costs), directly attacking your 900s trial timeout; redundancy-pruned samples also reduce the overlap problem §4 addresses.

## 4. Sample weighting — mostly obviated, cheap where it isn't

AFML ch.4 (average uniqueness = mean 1/c_t over the label's lifespan; return-attribution weights; sequential bootstrap). Independent quantitative validation is weak — mlfinlab demos show uniqueness rising 0.6→0.7 with sequential bootstrap, practitioner articles claim improvements, but no peer-reviewed effect size. Verdict for you: (a) the **meta dataset needs none** — `simulate_ticker` trades are non-overlapping per ticker by construction (uniqueness ≈ 1); only optional cross-ticker downweight 1/c_t for your 6 BTC-correlated cryptos; (b) your Optuna objective already evaluates non-overlapping holds — weights would only affect FIT. If you train on every-bar TBL labels, pass `sample_weight = avg_uniqueness x |TB_Ret|` to LightGBM (one parameter) and multiply into the LSTM's existing `|y|+1` loss weights. **Skip sequential bootstrap**: O(N²)-ish, Jetson-hostile, thinnest evidence. CUSUM sampling (§3) reduces concurrency at the source, which is the cleaner fix.

## 5. Quantile heads for tail-aware sizing

**Evidence.** LightGBM natively supports `objective='quantile', alpha=τ` (pinball loss). M5 Uncertainty (50k+ series): winner trained **gradient-boosted models per quantile** (WSPL 0.154), LightGBM dominating top ranks — the strongest cross-domain evidence that LGB-quantile is the practical SOTA at this compute class. In trading: FutureQuant Transformer (arXiv 2505.05595) reports +0.1193%/30-min trade vs point-forecast models from distributional outputs; Christoffersen & Diebold (Mgmt Sci 2006) show vol dynamics make *sign* probabilities forecastable at intermediate horizons. Trading-specific sizing evidence: suggestive, not established.

**Recipe.** Train two extra boosters (α=0.10, 0.90) in `train_lgb_ensemble` on the same flattened windows/`TB_Ret` target (~5–10 extra min weekly, few MB each). Live rules: skip/veto when `q10 < −stop_dist` (predicted 10%-tail breaches your ATR stop ⇒ high stop-hit probability); size multiplier ∝ `clip(q50/|q10|, 0, 1.3)`. Cheap, interpretable, and feeds the existing risk ladder. Defer LSTM pinball heads (3-output head + pinball loss) — touches hypersearch and JIT trace for less marginal value.

## 6. Classification vs regression at 12–48h

Leung/Daouk/Chen (Int. J. Forecasting 2000): classification beat level-estimation for trading returns on G7 indices. Christoffersen–Diebold: sign forecastability peaks at **intermediate horizons** (your 12–48h hourly band plausibly qualifies) and is largest when vol is dynamic — crypto especially. But Gu–Kelly–Xiu-style regression dominates cross-sectional work, and your regression output feeds threshold, Kelly, and the LLM gate. **The literature-supported answer is the hybrid you'd get from §1+§2: keep the Huber-regression primary (magnitude, ranking), add the meta-classifier (trade/no-trade + size).** Joubert's framework explicitly frames this as primary-regression + secondary-classification; don't rewrite the LSTM as a classifier.

## Execution order, files, and compute (8GB Jetson budget)

| # | Change | Files | Effort | Weekly compute |
|---|--------|-------|--------|----------------|
| 1 | Meta-label dataset + LGB meta + veto/size | new `build_meta_dataset.py`, `meta_model.py`; `backtest.py` (factor exit engine, emit features), `base_loop.py` (~line 1009/1168), `run_pipeline.py` | 2–3 d | +10–25 min replay, <100MB |
| 2 | `exit_path()` refactor + TB_Ret/TB_Label cols (EOD vertical for stocks) | `backtest.py`, both harvest scripts, `data_utils.py` validation | 1–2 d | +2 min, +25MB |
| 3 | `Target_Return_EOD` stock label + adaptive fb choice | `harvest_stock_data.py`, `adaptive_config.py` | 0.5 d | ~0 |
| 4 | A/B: LGB leg on TB_Ret vs raw return through policy gate | `hypersearch_v2.train_lgb_ensemble` | 0.5 d | ~0 |
| 5 | CUSUM train-row mask | harvest scripts, `hypersearch_v2.load_data/folds` | 0.5–1 d | **−60–80% epoch time** |
| 6 | q10/q90 LGB boosters + stop-breach veto | `model_lgb.py`, `hypersearch_v2.py`, `predict_now.py` | 1 d | +5–10 min |
| 7 | Uniqueness x return-attribution `sample_weight` (TBL rows only) | `hypersearch_v2.py`, `model_lgb.py` | 0.5 d | ~0 |

Expected effects (literature anchors, not promises): meta-labeling ≈ Sharpe x1.5–2 on real-trade datasets (0.36→0.74 Man & Chan) with fewer trades (less 0.60%/0.11% fee drag); TBL+CUSUM = the only net-of-cost-positive combo in the closest peer-reviewed crypto study; EOD stock labels remove a 2–7-day vs ≤6.5h target/policy mismatch that no amount of tuning can overcome.
topRecommendations: 1. Build the meta-labeling layer from your policy backtester (2-3 days): factor backtest.simulate_ticker's exit loop into a reusable exit_path() function, replay full history at 0.5x trade_threshold to emit one row per trade (label = net_pct>0, ~15 entry-bar features: predicted_return, ATR_Pct, vol, RSI, BB width, sentiment, regime flags, LSTM-LGB disagreement, hour-of-day, trailing hit-rate), train a depth-<=5 LightGBM classifier with isotonic calibration on a purged time split, and wire veto (p<0.5) + AFML sizing m=2*Phi((p-0.5)/sqrt(p(1-p)))-1 into base_loop beside kelly_mult (NOT inside the [0.1,1.3] tilt). Literature anchor: Sharpe 0.36->0.74 on 464 real trades (Man & Chan, ICAIF 2020).

2. Add exit-stack-matched triple-barrier labels (1-2 days): per bar, run exit_path with your live barriers (2.5x/2.0x ATR stop with floor/ceil, TP=min(tp_ceil, 2.0*stop_dist), trailing after +1.5%/+1%) and vertical barrier = fb bars for crypto, min(fb, same-day last bar) for stocks; emit TB_Ret_{fb} (continuous, keeps your Huber regression), TB_Label_{fb}, TB_ExitBars_{fb} in both harvest scripts. Single code path guarantees label==live-exit semantics.

3. Fix the stock label/policy mismatch immediately (0.5 day): current Target_Return_12..48 spans 1.8-7.4 trading days but live stock holds are <=6.3h due to 15:50 ET flatten; add Target_Return_EOD (entry close -> same-day last bar) and let the adaptive forward_bars search include it. Cheapest expected-value fix in the system.

4. A/B the LightGBM ensemble leg on TB_Ret vs raw forward return (0.5 day): retrain train_lgb_ensemble with the policy-consistent target and compare via the existing backtest.py --gate; promotes only if the policy-level Sharpe/DSR improves. Zero new infrastructure.

5. Add CUSUM event sampling for training rows (0.5-1 day): boolean CUSUM_Event column (S_t = max(0, S_{t-1}+r_t), trigger at h = EWMA daily vol or 0.75-1% crypto / 0.4-0.5% stock), intersect train indices with events in hypersearch load_data while keeping all bars for validation/holdout; expect 3-6x fewer train rows -> proportionally faster epochs on the Jetson, with the closest peer-reviewed crypto study finding CUSUM+TBL the only net-of-cost-positive combination.

6. Train q10/q90 LightGBM quantile boosters (1 day, +5-10 min weekly): objective='quantile' alpha=0.1/0.9 on the same flattened windows; live rule: veto when q10 < -stop_dist (predicted tail breaches the ATR stop), size multiplier proportional to clip(q50/|q10|,0,1.3). M5 Uncertainty evidence says per-quantile LGB is the practical SOTA at this compute class.

7. Pass sample_weight = average_uniqueness x |TB_Ret| to LightGBM and fold uniqueness into the LSTM's existing |y|+1 loss weighting for overlapping every-bar TBL labels only (0.5 day); skip it for the meta dataset (trades are non-overlapping per ticker by construction) and skip sequential bootstrap entirely (O(N^2), weakest evidence, Jetson-hostile).

8. Keep the regression primary; do NOT convert the LSTM to a classifier. The supported hybrid is regression primary + classification meta-layer (Joubert framework; Leung/Daouk/Chen direction-beats-level evidence is monthly-index scale; your Optuna objective already optimizes a trading metric).

9. Retrain the meta-model weekly in run_pipeline.py after the primary, and extend the policy gate to compare meta-on vs meta-off in the same simulate_ticker pass, rolling back the meta-model independently of the primary on failure.

10. Log exit-reason distribution from backtest.py (hard_stop/take_profit/trailing/eod_flatten/signal_sell shares) per asset class each week as the diagnostic for barrier-parameter drift between labels and live policy; if eod_flatten dominates stocks, shorten the stock fb search space.

# Portfolio Construction for the 10-Crypto + 10-Stock Long-Only Book

## Current state (code-verified)
- Per-symbol decisions; correlation tilt in `portfolio.py`: `factor = max(0.5, 1 - 0.5*avg_corr)` from a **30-bar**, per-asset-class corr matrix (no crypto-x-stock pairs; cache keyed by asset_type).
- Per-position GARCH sizing toward per-class annual targets (35%/18%) — this is already implicit inverse-vol sizing, but there is **no book-level realized-vol loop** and no book risk cap besides notional caps ($1k/$3k crypto, $5k stock clips).
- Breaker: 5% on **account** last_equity in both loops — so a combined breaker already exists de facto.
- `stock_loop.py:430` ranks preds, takes top 10 of ~47; line 476 sells only if out of top-10 **and** pred<0 (an implicit hold band on exit, but **no entry buffer**).

## 1. HRP / ERC vs inverse-vol vs 1/N for N≤20
Established: DeMiguel-Garlappi-Uppal (RFS 2009) — none of 14 optimizing models consistently beat 1/N out-of-sample; a 25-asset mean-variance portfolio needs ~3,000 months of data to win. Anything using estimated **means** is dead on arrival here. Volatilities are far more estimable; correlations sit in between. Under covariance misspecification, inverse-vol (IV) portfolios are the most robust, followed by HRP (MDPI Risks 2019); ReSolve/InvestResolve report EW and IV among the best ex-post performers while max-Sharpe/min-var degrade. HRP beats Markowitz out-of-sample, but reported shortfalls vs naive EW/IV appear precisely with **highly correlated asset groups** — your case. HRP's known failure modes: linkage sensitivity (single-linkage chaining concentrates weight in a few assets; Ward needed for diversification) and meaningless hierarchies when N≈10 forms one cluster (crypto book = one BTC-beta cluster). Burggraf (Finance Research Letters 2021) finds HRP improves **tail-adjusted** returns on crypto, but on a *large* universe where hierarchy exists. ERC ≈ IV when correlations are homogeneous — which they are within each of your books. **Verdict: IV (which you nearly have) ≈ HRP/ERC for this book; skip the dendrogram.** Minimum viable estimation: 20-60d EWMA for vols; ≥90-120 daily bars for correlations (SE(ρ)≈(1−ρ²)/√T: at ρ=0.7, 30 bars → ±0.09, 120 → ±0.05). Your 30-bar matrix is the weakest link.

## 2. Book-level vol targeting
Established: Moreira-Muir (JF 2017) scale factor *portfolios* by k/RV² of the prior month — large alphas and Sharpe gains for market/momentum/profitability. Harvey-Hoyle et al. (JPM 2018; 60 assets, 1926-2017, 10% target): Sharpe gains **only for "risk assets" (equities, credit)** via the leverage effect, but left-tail and drawdown reduction across *all* assets — and your whole book is risk assets. QuantPedia's replication: EWMA(20d) targeting on 60/40 lifted Sharpe 1.02→1.34 and cut vol 10.59%→8.09%; EWMA beat simple 20d SD; weekly rebalanced, leverage capped at 2. Honest caveat: Cederburg et al. (JFE 2020, 103 strategies) show real-time vol-managed versions often don't beat unmanaged on Sharpe (spanning-regression instability) — exceptions include momentum-like factors. So sell this internally as **drawdown/tail control with possible Sharpe upside**, not guaranteed alpha.

Recipe for this system: daily, compute book realized vol as EWMA (λ=0.94, RiskMetrics ≈20d center of mass) of daily account-equity returns from `GET /v2/account/portfolio/history`; m = clip(target_book_vol / σ_book, 0.5, 1.5); multiply all *new* entry notionals by m; only trim existing positions when m<0.7 (band per Daryanani 20%-relative-band logic to stop churn). Set target from your measured 60d account vol (likely 12-18% given ~50-60% deployment); start at 15% annualized. **No double-counting with per-position GARCH**: position-level scaling normalizes cross-section, book-level normalizes the aggregate — the standard two-layer managed-futures stack (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen size each position at 40%/σ, then portfolio-level vol drives most of TSMOM's benefit per Kim-Tse-Wald 2016). Guard the stack: total multiplier = clip(tilt × m, 0.1, 1.5), and make the book layer *slower* (20d EWMA) than per-bar GARCH so they don't both spike on the same shock.

## 3. One risk budget across crypto + stocks
BTC-Nasdaq 20d correlation peaked ~0.87 in 2024; through late 2025 BTC decoupled on the **upside** while still "tumbling during risk-off phases" — the bearish correlation is the one that survives. High-beta tech + crypto is one trade in the left tail. Your 5% breaker already watches combined account equity (good — keep). Gaps: (a) the correlation matrix never sees cross-book pairs — BTC-ETH vs your high-beta names will read 0.0 and the tilt under-penalizes; (b) vol targeting is per-class only. Fix: one combined 120-day daily-return correlation matrix (daily bars sidestep the asynchronous-session problem; hourly crypto vs RTH stocks gives garbage), one book-vol scalar m from total equity applied in both loops, and a soft de-risk band: intraday account DD ≥3.5% → force m=0.5 before the 5% hard halt.

## 4. Long-only de-risking: cash beats inverse ETFs
Inverse/levered ETFs carry statistically negative alpha (−0.62%/mo CAPM, −0.50%/mo Carhart), 0.89-1.01% ERs, and daily-reset volatility decay; fine for day-scale hedges, value-destroying as a standing sleeve. With no shorting edge in your models, **scaling to cash via m is strictly cheaper**. Cash parking: Alpaca live pays 3.6% APR (3.56% APY) on idle USD with no minimum — vs SGOV 30-day SEC yield 3.53% (May 28, 2026). **A wash live**, and SGOV would pollute flatten/breaker/buying-power logic. Paper accounts earn nothing — so add a synthetic ~3.5% accrual on idle cash in performance *reporting* for paper-vs-live comparability instead of trading SGOV.

## 5. Turnover control
Novy-Marx-Velikov (RFS 2016): a **buy/hold spread** (buy at a tight rank, keep holding at a looser rank) is the single most effective cost mitigation; strategies under ~50%/mo one-way turnover survive 20-57bp costs. Morningstar-style implementations hold while in the top half. Daryanani: 20% *relative* drift bands beat 10/15/25% for rebalancing. Concrete for `stock_loop`: enter only at rank ≤7 of 47; hold while rank ≤15 (keep the existing pred<0 exit); require a new entrant's pred to exceed the weakest incumbent's by ≥2× round-trip cost (0.22%) before displacement. Expect roughly one-third to one-half fewer marginal swaps at ~$5.50 saved per avoided $5k round trip, plus less slippage and fewer LLM-gate calls.

## 6. Concentration math
For N equal assets at avg pairwise ρ: ENB = N/(1+(N−1)ρ). Crypto at ρ=0.7/0.8/0.9 → **1.37 / 1.22 / 1.10 effective bets** (top-30 coins run 0.6-0.95 to BTC; your "2-3 bets" intuition is generous — it's nearer 1.2-1.4). Stocks at ρ≈0.55 → ~1.7. Combined, with 0.5-0.65 cross-block risk-off correlation → ~2-2.5 bets total. Stop-risk aggregation: 10 crypto positions each risking 0.5% to stop at ρ=0.8 ≈ 0.5%×√(10·(1+9·0.8)) = **4.5% book equity-at-stop** — nearly your whole 5% breaker from one cluster (vs 1.6% if independent). Two fixes: cap per-book aggregate stop-risk at Σrᵢ·√((1+(N−1)ρ̄)/N) ≤ 2.5% (auto-shrinks per-trade risk toward 0.25% or holds ~5 names at ρ̄=0.8), and replace the tilt with the variance-consistent factor = 1/√(1+n·ρ̄) (n = existing positions): at n=9, ρ̄=0.8 → 0.35× (your current floor of 0.5 is ~40% too generous exactly when it matters).

## Recommended minimal stack
Keep IV-style sizing you already have → fix correlation estimation (120d, cross-book) → add the book-level EWMA vol scalar on combined equity → ENB-aware book risk caps + tilt → rank-buffered top-10. Total ~3-4 days of work, no new dependencies, negligible Jetson load (one 20×20 daily corr matrix + one EWMA). Skip HRP/ERC, inverse ETFs, and SGOV.

Book-level vol scalar (combined account): daily EWMA λ=0.94 on equity returns from GET /v2/account/portfolio/history; m = clip(0.15/σ_book, 0.5, 1.5) multiplying all new entry notionals in BOTH loops; trim existing positions only when m<0.7; cap tilt×m ≤ 1.5. 2. ENB-based book risk cap: from the cached corr matrix compute ρ̄ per book; block/shrink entries so Σ(stop-risk_i)·√((1+(N−1)ρ̄)/N) ≤ 2.5% per book (≤4% combined). At ρ̄=0.8 the current 10×0.5% crypto book carries ~4.5% equity-at-stop — nearly the whole 5% breaker. Effort ~0.5-1 day. Highest risk-reduction per line of code.

3. Combined cross-book correlation matrix: extend portfolio.py to one 'combined' cache over 120 DAILY bars (not 30 hourly) including BTC/ETH × stock symbols; apply the existing gate and sizing tilt across books. SE(ρ) drops ~0.09→0.05. Effort ~0.5-1 day.

Rank-buffer the top-10 stock selection (Novy-Marx-Velikov buy/hold spread — the single most effective cost mitigation): enter only at rank ≤7 of 47; hold while rank ≤15 (keep the pred<0 exit at stock_loop.py:476); displace incumbents only if new pred − weakest incumbent pred ≥ 0.22% (2× round trip). Effort 2-4 hours; expect ~30-50% fewer marginal swaps.

7. Soft de-risk band ahead of the breaker: intraday combined-account drawdown ≥3.5% forces m=0.5 (entries shrink, optional trims) before the existing 5% hard halt; resets with the 16:05 ET baseline. Effort ~2 hours.

# Model Lifecycle: Monitoring + Lifecycle Design for the Jetson Trader

## 1. Concept-drift monitoring (what to compute, exact thresholds, actions)
You already log every decision with `pred_return` to `journals/*.jsonl` (`/Users/kywwilson/Desktop/Projects/trader/trade_journal.py`) and have an atomic retrain trigger (`_check_retrain_trigger`, `run_pipeline.py:57`) plus a circuit breaker. That is 90% of the plumbing; the missing piece is a daily monitor job (numpy-only, <100MB, fine alongside the 2.5GB stack) computing three detector families:

**(a) Prediction-distribution PSI.** At train time, store decile edges of the champion's holdout predictions (add to the manifest in `save_model_atomically`, `hypersearch_v2.py:959`). Daily, compute PSI of trailing-7-day live `pred_return`s vs those bins, per asset class (~240 crypto + ~220 stock predictions/day, so 7 days ≈ 1,500-3,300 samples — enough; PSI is unstable under ~500 samples). Industry-standard thresholds, originating in credit scorecards and confirmed across Fiddler/Minitab/Arthur/DataRobot docs: **PSI < 0.1 stable; 0.1-0.25 watch; ≥ 0.25 action**. Rule: PSI ≥ 0.25 for 2 consecutive days → write `retrain_trigger.json` (unscheduled retrain through the normal DSR+policy gates).

**(b) Feature PSI** vs training decile edges (store with the scaler). Alarm if ≥3 of ~23 features ≥0.25, or any ≥0.5. Diagnostic matrix: pred-PSI high + feature-PSI low → model/serving bug (investigate, don't retrain); both high → regime change (retrain); feature-PSI high + pred-PSI low → monitor.

**(c) CUSUM on live hit rate and per-trade expectancy.** Fixed-horizon tests are hopeless at your trade rate: detecting a 52%→50% hit-rate drop at α=0.05/80% power needs ~9,800 trades/arm (1-3 years at 10-30 trades/day); even 55%→50% needs ~1,560. Sequential detection is the standard answer (CUSUM/Page-Hinkley emphasize sustained drift; ADWIN auto-windows — all available in `river`, a tiny pure-Python dependency, or ~50 lines hand-rolled). Concrete recipe: take p0 = hit rate from the policy-backtest gate's holdout replay; run tabular CUSUM S_t = max(0, S_{t-1} + (p0 − hit_t − k)) with allowance k = 0.04 (half of the 8pp shift you want to catch); tune threshold h by simulating on historical journals for ARL0 ≈ 500 trades (~1 false alarm/month at 20 trades/day). Run a parallel CUSUM on net-R expectancy.

**Stand-down rule (fail-closed):** CUSUM alarm AND pred-PSI ≥ 0.25 → halt new entries via the existing circuit-breaker path until a retrain passes the holdout + policy gates. CUSUM alarm alone → halve Kelly fraction and trigger retrain. PSI alone → retrain, keep trading.

## 2. Alpha-decay evidence: what to expect
Established (monthly-horizon factors): McLean & Pontiff (J. Finance 2016, 97 predictors) measure **26% return decay out-of-sample and 58% post-publication**. Wiecki et al. (SSRN 2016, 888 Quantopian algos) find backtest Sharpe has **R² < 0.025** for predicting out-of-sample Sharpe — the single most relevant number for your promotion gates: holdout Sharpe is a weak forecast of live Sharpe, which justifies ensembling + shadow testing over winner-takes-all. A 2026 arXiv preprint (AI-driven alpha decay) claims medium-frequency factor half-life compressed to ~18 months, but that's a calibrated model, not measurement — treat as speculation. **No credible published decay-rate exists for hourly-horizon retail-scale ML signals**; the practical implication is to assume live edge ≈ 50-70% of holdout and alarm (CUSUM above) when the live-vs-holdout Sharpe gap exceeds ~50% for 2+ weeks.

## 3. Ensemble-across-checkpoints: do it, K=3-4, equal weights
Evidence: Gu-Kelly-Xiu (RFS 2020) average **10 identically-specified networks with different seeds** at every re-estimation date specifically for variance reduction — the canonical empirical-asset-pricing practice. The forecast-combination literature ("combination puzzle": Genre et al. 2013; Claeskens et al.) robustly shows **equal weights beat estimated optimal weights** out-of-sample because weight estimation error dominates. Snapshot ensembles (Huang et al., ICLR 2017) and stacked LSTM snapshot ensembles (Springer 2019) show cyclic-LR checkpoint ensembles beat a single optimized LSTM at zero extra training cost; typical time-series error reductions are modest (~3-5% RMSE) but the bigger win for you is **promotion de-risking**: a bad new champion gets weight 1/K instead of 1.0.

Design: keep the last K=4 gate-passing weekly champions in a `models/registry/` dir (your `.prev` copy mechanism already half-does this). Memory: max config (hidden 384, 2 layers) ≈ 1.8M params ≈ 7MB fp32 → 4 LSTMs + 4 LGB ensembles < 60MB. Inference is hourly and pooled (`base_loop.py:618`) — 4x cost is trivial. **Critical system-specific detail:** `forward_bars` and `trade_threshold` are tuned per model, so raw `pred_return` averaging across checkpoints is invalid. Either pin `forward_bars` per asset class, or average the normalized score s_i = pred_i/threshold_i and trade when mean(s) > 1. Drop any member whose own pred-PSI alarms. Expected effect with inter-checkpoint prediction correlation ρ≈0.7: ensemble std factor √(1/K + (1−1/K)ρ) ≈ 0.88 → ~10-12% prediction-noise reduction, plus fat-tail protection on bad-model weeks. Cheaper complement: SWA (`torch.optim.swa_utils`) over the final training epochs of the winning config — a free intra-run ensemble with zero inference overhead.

## 4. Retrain cadence: keep weekly, add triggers, A/B the window
Published guidance for hourly-horizon trading models is thin; walk-forward practice uses 1-3yr in-sample/1-6mo out-of-sample, and the cost-aware retraining literature (Cara, KBS 2024; "When to retrain", arXiv 2505.14903) frames it as staleness-cost vs retrain-cost — with your free Jetson compute, the binding costs are promotion risk and device contention, not dollars. Recommendation: **keep weekly scheduled retrains** (your gates make over-frequent retraining safe-ish), add the §1 drift triggers for unscheduled retrains, and resolve rolling-vs-expanding empirically: literature on crypto regime shifts weakly favors rolling 12-18mo for crypto and expanding for stocks, but it's regime-dependent — run a quarterly A/B inside your existing purged walk-forward comparing expanding vs rolling-18mo on crypto and log fold Sharpes. Don't shorten below weekly: with ~140 effective independent observations/week (see §7) you cannot tell a good weekly model from a lucky one, which is exactly why K-ensembling beats faster cadence.

## 5. Online/incremental learning: LGB refit yes (gated), LSTM no
**LightGBM:** `Booster.refit()` keeps tree structure and re-blends leaf values: leaf = 0.9·old + 0.1·new at the default `refit_decay_rate=0.9` (LightGBM docs). This is a cheap, low-risk daily "leaf recalibration" on trailing ~30 days between weekly full retrains — structure is frozen so it behaves like damped recalibration, unlike `init_model` continued training which appends trees and drifts the model. Worth a gated experiment (compare refit-daily vs static champion in the policy replay). **LSTM:** Ash & Adams (NeurIPS 2020) show warm-started networks **generalize worse than retrained-from-scratch** despite similar training loss; the shrink-and-perturb fix (θ ← λθ + γθ_init) exists, but at weekly full-Optuna cadence online LSTM updates add operational risk for little gain — skip. **River** is the right tool for its drift detectors (ADWIN/PageHinkley, tiny footprint), not for replacing your models; its per-row dict design is built for streaming metrics, and there is no published evidence of river-class online regressors beating periodically-retrained batch models in trading.

## 6. Optuna study lifecycle
You version studies and use `load_if_exists=True` with TPE (`hypersearch_v2.py:1148-1154`). Stale-prior best practice: **start a fresh study quarterly (or on any feature-set/data-regime change) and warm-start via `study.enqueue_trial()` with the top-5 configs from the prior study** — transfers knowledge without TPE density built on stale data. (OptunaHub's Meta-Learn TPE does task-similarity warm-starting formally; overkill here.) Set `TPESampler(multivariate=True, group=True)` — documented to improve TPE on conditional/structured spaces like yours. Multi-objective: TPE and NSGA-II both support Sharpe+maxDD Pareto fronts (Optuna docs recommend TPE/GP under 1,000 trials), and NSGA-II Sharpe/MaxDD trading studies exist — but Pareto fronts break unattended auto-promotion (many non-dominated trials, human must choose). Cleaner for your pipeline: keep the scalar `mean − 0.5·std` objective and add max-DD as a **constraint** (`TPESampler(constraints_func=...)`, e.g. holdout policy-replay DD ≤ 15%) or a hinge penalty.

## 7. Champion/challenger shadow deployment + power analysis
Standard MLOps shadow pattern (DataRobot/H2O/Dataiku): challenger scores every request, champion alone trades, both logged. Recipe for your code: `save_model_atomically` writes the gate-passing candidate to `{prefix}challenger/` instead of replacing the champion; `_get_predictions` loads both and `log_decision` gains a `challenger_pred` field. ~1-2 days work, 2x hourly inference (trivial).

**Power analysis — the honest numbers.** Trade-level comparison is underpowered: at 10-30 trades/day, a 5pp hit-rate edge needs ~1,560 trades/arm (2-5 months); Sharpe-difference tests are worse — Portfolio Optimizer's worked PSR/MinTRL-difference example shows that after **52 weeks**, P(true SR_challenger > SR_champion) ≈ 48%, i.e., a coin flip; the correlation term in the SR-difference variance is the only thing that saves you (ρ≈0.95+ between champion/challenger shrinks required n ~20x, still months). Therefore compare at the **forecast level on paired bars**: Diebold-Mariano test (Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold small-sample correction; valid from ~20 obs but use HAC lag ≥ `forward_bars` because your 12-48h labels overlap) on squared error and sign accuracy. Volume: ~460/day logged forecasts → 14 days ≈ 6,400 pairs, but overlap (÷24) and cross-symbol correlation give **n_eff ≈ 40-70 in 2 weeks, ~100-140 in 4 weeks** — detects standardized loss-diff effects ≈0.4 (2wk) / ≈0.28 (4wk). Promotion rule: **14-day minimum, 28-day standard shadow**; promote into the K-ensemble (weight 1/K — graceful, resolves the power problem structurally) if (1) HLN-DM shows challenger not significantly worse + better point estimate on both metrics, (2) policy-replay on the shadow window (your existing `backtest.py --gate` machinery, run prospectively instead of retrospectively) shows net P&L ≥ champion − 1 SE, (3) PSR-difference probability reported but not gated (underpowered). Trade-level stats over the shadow window serve as sanity checks (expectancy sign), not significance tests.

## 8. Memory/runtime budget (Jetson 8GB)
K=4 LSTM+LGB registry < 60MB; challenger duplicate < 15MB; monitor job (numpy PSI + CUSUM over JSONL) < 100MB transient, daily cron; river detectors negligible. Skip Evidently/NannyML in-process (plotly/pandas-heavy) — hand-rolled PSI is ~30 lines. Total added steady-state: well under 200MB.
topRecommendations: 1. Daily drift-monitor job (numpy-only): PSI of live pred_return vs champion holdout deciles + per-feature PSI vs training deciles, thresholds 0.1 warn / 0.25 action (2 consecutive days -> write retrain_trigger.json, reusing run_pipeline.py:57 mechanism). Store decile edges in the model manifest at save time. Effort: 1-2 days. Impact: catches model/regime breakage days-to-weeks before the next scheduled retrain; near-zero false-positive cost since the trigger goes through existing DSR+policy gates.

2. CUSUM monitors on live hit rate and per-trade net-R expectancy vs the policy-backtest holdout baseline (allowance k=0.04, threshold h tuned on historical journals for ARL0~500 trades). Alarm+PSI>=0.25 -> stand down entries via existing circuit breaker; alarm alone -> halve Kelly fraction + trigger retrain. Effort: 1 day. Impact: principled unscheduled-retrain/stand-down rule; fixed-horizon tests would need ~9,800 trades to catch a 2pp hit-rate drop.

3. Challenger shadow mode: gate-passing candidate saved to challenger/ path instead of replacing champion; base_loop scores both, journals gain challenger_pred. 14-day minimum / 28-day standard shadow. Effort: 1-2 days. Impact: eliminates winner-takes-all promotion risk that Wiecki et al. quantify (backtest Sharpe R^2<0.025 for live performance).

4. Promotion statistics module: HLN-corrected Diebold-Mariano non-inferiority on paired squared-error and sign accuracy (HAC lag >= forward_bars for overlapping labels) + prospective policy replay on the shadow window + PSR/Sharpe-difference probability (report-only). Effort: 1 day. Impact: statistically honest promotion at n_eff~40-140; prevents both premature promotion and indefinite shadow.

5. K=4 equal-weight checkpoint ensemble of the last gate-passing weekly champions (registry dir extending the existing .prev pattern), averaging threshold-normalized scores pred_i/threshold_i (forward_bars differs per model — raw averaging is invalid); drop members whose pred-PSI alarms. Effort: 1-2 days, <60MB RAM. Impact: ~10-12% prediction-noise reduction at rho~0.7 (GKX-style seed-ensemble evidence) and 1/K exposure to any single bad model.

6. Add SWA (torch.optim.swa_utils) over the final training epochs of the winning Optuna config before save_model_atomically — free intra-run ensemble, zero inference cost. Effort: 0.5-1 day. Impact: small but consistent generalization gain (snapshot-ensemble literature, ~3-5% error reduction in time-series studies).

7. Optuna hygiene: quarterly fresh study warm-started via study.enqueue_trial(top-5 configs of prior study); set TPESampler(multivariate=True, group=True); add holdout max-DD as a constraint (constraints_func) rather than a second objective so auto-promotion stays unattended. Effort: 0.5-1 day. Impact: removes stale-prior TPE bias after regime/feature changes while keeping sample efficiency.

8. Daily LightGBM leaf recalibration experiment: Booster.refit() on trailing ~30 days (default refit_decay_rate=0.9, structure frozen), gated by the policy replay vs the static champion. Effort: 1 day. Impact: cheap mid-week adaptation; low risk because tree structure is fixed. Decision: do NOT online-fine-tune the LSTM (Ash & Adams: warm-starting degrades generalization; shrink-and-perturb only if ever needed).

9. Quarterly rolling(12-18mo)-vs-expanding training-window A/B inside the existing purged walk-forward for crypto (expanding likely fine for stocks); adopt per-asset-class winner. Effort: 1 day setup. Impact: resolves the lookback question empirically — literature gives no reliable answer at hourly horizons.

10. Set live-performance expectations from evidence: assume live edge ~50-70% of holdout (McLean-Pontiff 26-58% decay; Wiecki et al.), encode holdout_sharpe*0.7 as the monitor baseline, and treat a >50% live-vs-holdout Sharpe gap sustained 2+ weeks as a drift signal feeding recommendation 2. Effort: hours. Impact: prevents both panic-retraining on normal decay and complacency on real breakage.

# Execution Microstructure Findings (retail $250–$5k clips, Alpaca)

Current stack (verified in repo): `compute_limit_price()` = mid+5bps buy limit, `manage_order_lifecycle(timeout=30)` → cancel → market fallback (`order_utils.py:83,178`); stock flatten at 15:50 with offset_bps=10 limit then market (`stock_loop.py:42-43,307`); `fees.py` already models maker=15bps but loops never use it.

## 1. Passive crypto entries: the largest lever (~15–20bps/round-trip)

**Fee facts (primary source, Alpaca docs):** tier-1 maker 15bps / taker 25bps; maker = order resting on the book, taker = market or *marketable* limit. Crypto supports only `gtc`/`ioc` TIF — **no post-only flag**, so "join the bid, never improve past it" is the way to guarantee non-marketable submission.

**Evidence that patience pays at your horizon:**
- Anand, Samadi, Sokobin (FINRA) & Venkataraman, *Retail Limit Orders* (Review of Finance 2025, 19-broker FINRA order data): retail limit orders cost ~**10bps less** than marketable orders (~20bps in small caps), ~**65% fully fill**, typically resting **>20 minutes** — patient liquidity supply works for retail in the current market structure.
- *Market Maker's Dilemma* (arXiv 2502.18625, 232,897 live Binance BTC-perp orders): adverse selection at the touch ≈ **−0.8bp unconditional at 1s horizon**. For sub-minute round trips that kills market-making; for your 12–48h hold it is noise. Your signal's drift over a 30-min execution window is only ~2–3bps (a 100–150bp 24h prediction × 0.5/24), far below the 20–30bps you save by not crossing — **patience is approximately free alpha at your horizon**.
- Fill math: with BTC 30-min vol ≈ 40–60bps, a bid resting ≤10bps below mid is touched with ~75–90% probability (reflection principle, near-zero drift) — consistent with the 65% retail full-fill benchmark.
- Cont & Kukanov (arXiv 1210.1625) formalize the optimal structure: passive first, convert remainder to aggressive as the non-execution penalty binds — i.e., your existing limit→market fallback is right, the 30s deadline is wrong by ~30×.

**Concrete tactic** (1–2 days, `order_utils.py` + `crypto_loop.py`): buy = join best bid (`gtc`); reprice (cancel/replace) every 60s if bid moved >1 tick (Hummingbot PMM default refresh is 60s; faster repricing adds little for non-HFT — Lehalle & Mounjid, arXiv 1610.00261, show imbalance-timing value is *eroded by latency*, so don't try to be clever, just follow the bid); hard deadline **15 min**, then IOC-marketable sweep; early escape to taker if price > arrival-mid + 0.25×ATR(1h) (signal running away). Use the existing `order_stream` cache instead of 2s REST polls. Expected per entry vs today (taker-ish at ~ask): fee delta 10bps + spread capture ~8–15bps on ~75% of entries, minus ~5–10bps chase on the rest ≈ **+12–15bps/entry**; applying the same to non-stop exits (TP/time exits, not stops) adds ~5–8bps → crypto round trip drops from your modeled 60bps to ~**40–45bps**. Feed realized maker share per symbol into `fees.round_trip_cost_pct(maker=...)` so `required_edge_pct` (2× cost) falls from ~1.3% toward ~0.85% — more trades legally pass the gate, but only as fast as measured maker share supports it.

**Ladders:** at $1k clips impact is nil; a 2-slice ladder (half at bid, half at bid−0.3×spread or +5min) mainly reduces entry-price variance. Worth ~2–5bps; optional, do after the single-level tactic works.

**Paper-trading caveat:** Alpaca paper fills limits against the quote with no queue modeling — haircut observed paper maker-fill rates ~10–20% when calibrating.

## 2. Time-of-bar effects: real, small, free to capture (~1–3bps)

- *Turn-of-the-candle* (Finance Research Letters / PMC10015199): BTC returns concentrate **at 15-min boundary minutes (0.55–0.66bp/min, t>9 across 7 exchanges since 2020)**; other minutes average negative. Buying exactly at the hourly close buys into the boundary spike; minutes after are systematically cheaper for buys.
- *Periodicity in Cryptocurrency Volatility and Liquidity* (arXiv 2109.12142): within-hour vol/volume patterns tied to algo activity and **futures funding times**, strengthening over time.
- Funding (00/08/16 UTC): direct spot-price-at-funding evidence is thin (label: weak/speculative); vol/volume clustering at these hours is documented. Avoidance is nearly free.

**Tactic** (hours): never submit in minute 0 of the hour; place the passive bid at minute 2–5 (it then rests through any post-turn fade); skip new submissions ±3 min around 00/08/16 UTC. Expected ~1–3bps plus avoiding boundary spread spikes.

## 3. Implementation shortfall feedback loop (builds on your planned IS item)

Perold (1988) decomposition adapted per trade — log in `trade_journal.py`: (a) **decision price** = close of the triggering hourly bar; (b) **arrival mid** at submission → *delay cost* = arrival − decision; (c) fill VWAP vs arrival mid → *spread/impact cost*; (d) fees from CFEE/FEE activities; (e) *opportunity/chase cost* = (fallback fill − original limit) × unfilled qty, and for abandoned trades the hypothetical 24h paper P&L; (f) flags: maker/taker, slice, time-to-fill, spread & depth at submission. IS = (a→fill all-in) signed by side.

**Switching thresholds:** no canonical literature numbers exist (honest gap — Cont-Kukanov gives the *structure*: aggressiveness ↑ with non-execution penalty). Use self-calibrated rules benchmarked to the 65% retail fill rate: per symbol, rolling 20 entries — maker fill rate <50% → tighten to mid; <30% or chase cost > (10bps + captured spread) → go marketable immediately; 20-trade mean IS > 2× modeled cost → alert + revert tactic. Effort ~1 day on top of the IS logging you already planned.

## 4. Spread/liquidity gates: add absolute caps + depth scaling

Evidence: BTC-USDT spread **more than doubles on weekends (1.2 → 2.8bps on majors)**, volumes −20–40% (Kaiko-derived); top-10bps book depth peaks ~11:00 UTC and is **−42% by 21:00 UTC** (Amberdata); Alpaca's own venue is thinner and has produced pathological spreads (2.5% BTC reported in 2021, Alpaca forum). Your edge-vs-spread gate scales with spread but a fat-tail print can still pass if predicted edge is large — and quote staleness makes huge spreads untrustworthy.

**Tactic** (0.5–1 day): absolute caps — skip entry if spread > 30bps (BTC/ETH), > 75bps (alts), tune after 2 weeks of logging (you can snapshot via the free Latest Orderbook REST + orderbook websocket); clip ≤ 10–20% of top-3-level depth on your side; halve crypto clips 20:00–24:00 UTC and weekends. Mostly tail insurance: prevents rare 50–250bp slippage entries; also harmless because passive tactic already earns spread when wide-but-real.

Stock caveat: free Alpaca data = **IEX only (~2% of volume)** — quoted spreads systematically wider than NBBO. Calibrate stock spread caps to IEX levels (or gate on spread relative to symbol's trailing median, not absolute), and measure stock IS vs fills, not vs IEX quotes.

## 5. Stock open and close

**Open:** Berkman, Koch, Tuttle & Zhang (JFQA 2012): opening prices are systematically **high vs rest of day, concentrated in high-attention/retail-heavy stocks** (= your high-beta universe); implicit cost of buying near the open "frequently exceeds the effective half spread." Spreads are widest at open and normalize within 15–30 min (multiple markets). Intraday-momentum evidence (Gao-Han-Li-Zhou, JFE 2018) is about first-half-hour *predicting* the close, not about open execution quality — using 9:30–9:45 *information* is fine; *buying* in 9:30–9:45 is expensive. **Tactic** (hours): start buy submissions at 9:45 (window stays 9:30–11:00 for signal computation), or require spread ≤ 1.5× trailing 20-day median before 10:00. Saves several bps on hot names, occasionally much more.

**Close:** Alpaca supports `cls` TIF (MOC/LOC) — submit by **15:50 ET** or it rejects until 19:00. The closing auction is the deepest liquidity event in US equities (**9.4–12.4% of daily volume**, record sizes 2024–2026, BMLL/NYSE), executing at the official close with zero spread. Replace the 15:50 limit-then-market flatten with MOC submitted ~15:45; saves ~3–8bps/position and removes market-fallback slippage. **Critical caveat:** Alpaca *paper* fills CLS like a quote-priced market order (documented 12–43bp biases) — implement behind a live-mode flag; in paper, keep current flatten but log slippage vs the official close from daily bars to quantify the benefit you'd capture live. Keep the GTC-stop-protected overnight sleeve logic unchanged (MOC only for the flattened remainder).

## 6. Quote imbalance: don't

Three independent sources agree top-of-book imbalance predicts seconds-to-~1-minute moves but **does not survive costs or latency for slow traders**: Market Maker's Dilemma (imbalance-maker −0.47bp, imbalance-taker −1.96bp per trade net), Lehalle & Mounjid (imbalance value eroded by latency; slow traders should place conservatively), and order-flow studies ("not strong enough… does not beat transaction costs"). At 12–48h horizons it's noise. Use the book **only** for: depth-aware clip sizing, spread caps (sec. 4), and optionally suppressing a reprice-chase when the opposite side is stacked. Zero effort: this is a decision not to build.

## Expected aggregate effect

Crypto round-trip ~60bps → ~40–45bps (items 1, 2, 4); stock entry cost −5–10bps (items 5, 9) and flatten −3–8bps live (MOC). Because `fees.py` documents costs as "the binding constraint," the second-order effect — lower `required_edge_pct` admitting more trades — is likely worth more than the direct savings. Sequence: IS logging first (week 1), passive crypto tactic (week 1–2), gates/timing (week 2), MOC flag + stock tweaks (week 3), then let the per-symbol switching thresholds manage tactics automatically.

Modify compute_limit_price/manage_order_lifecycle in order_utils.py. Effort: 1-2 days. Impact: +12-15bps per entry (10bps fee delta + spread capture × ~75% fill rate, net of chase).

Per-symbol rolling-20 rules: maker fill <50% → price at mid; <30% or chase > savings → taker; mean IS > 2× modeled cost → alert+revert. Effort: 1 day (extends planned IS item).
